subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw expose an ordinary plugin runtime caller for plugin-registered Gateway methods, and should that surface be raw dispatch, an allowlisted request API, or typed service/capability contracts?
rationale: This changes the public Plugin SDK and Gateway authorization boundary, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API shape or security model.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
options.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep route-scoped dispatch only
options.body: Decline ordinary plugin-to-plugin Gateway calls for now and direct plugins to existing HTTP route or purpose-built capability seams.

options.title: Allow raw Gateway dispatch
options.body: Expose a generic method-string caller and accept the larger compatibility and security surface as a maintainer-owned product decision.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current route-scoped dispatch contract and is the strongest history match for the Gateway/Plugin SDK boundary.
